1: # The run contract of the opene902 timing probe: what a Site must bind before this pack can run,
2: # what a generation produces inside the Campaign workspace, and what the pack runs on the Site.
3: # `/hima pack check <pack> --site <site>` reads this file against a Site's own and reports every
4: # input that is not bound, every wrapper the Permit will not run, and every rule or reader that does
5: # not exist.
6: id: opene902-timing-probe
7: version: '2'
8: title: opene902 timing probe
9: 
10: # What a Site binds, in its site file under `bindings:`. The same pack runs on another Site by
11: # editing that file, never this one.
12: inputs:
13:   - name: flowRoot
14:     description: >-
15:       The Golden Flow's root on the Site: the directory holding the makefile the flow is driven by.
16:       Read-only to a Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of it, never here.
17:   - name: design
18:     description: The design the flow builds, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
19:   - name: workspaceRoot
20:     description: >-
21:       Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing
22:       the pack does writes anywhere else.
23: 
24: # What a generation leaves in its Campaign workspace. Paths are relative to the workspace, with
25: # `${design}` bound from the Site's binding of that input.
26: outputs:
27:   - name: qorReport
28:     path: flow/results/${design}/syn/report/qor.rpt
29:     reader: dc-qor-report
30:     description: The Design Compiler qor report of the generation just synthesized. The judged report.
31:   - name: synthesisLog
32:     path: flow/logs/${design}/dc_shell.log
33:     description: What dc_shell said while it ran. Read by a person after a failure, not by a reader.
34: 
35: # What the Site must let this pack run: the first word of every tool's command line. The Permit's
36: # `allowedWrappers` decides each one, so a pack cannot introduce a command a Site owner never allowed.
37: environment:
38:   wrappers:
39:     - make
40: 
41: # How a Campaign workspace is prepared from the bound flow root, once per Campaign. The copy lands in
42: # `<workspace>/flow/`, which is the pack anatomy's fixed place for it (see README, "Pack anatomy").
43: workspace:
44:   copy:
45:     - Makefile
46:     - flows
47:     - manifests
48:     - tools
49:     - build/${design}
50:     - sources/${design}
51: 
52: # The pack's tools. Each names the file a person reads and runs by hand, and the command line the
53: # fabric launches on the Site. `${NAME}` in `argv` is one of the tool's declared `inputs`, which are
54: # the environment variables the tool's own script reads.
55: tools:
56:   - id: synth
57:     file: tools/synth.sh
58:     description: >-
59:       One synthesis generation at a chosen clock period, inside the Campaign's own copy of the flow.
60:       `FORCE_SYNTH=1` so no generation ever reuses another's netlist, and `EDA_CONTAINER_NAME` so the
61:       copy is bound into a container of this Campaign's own — running it under the Site's container
62:       name would write the Site's own results.
63:     inputs: [WORKSPACE, FLOW_ROOT, DESIGN, PERIOD_NS, CAMPAIGN]
64:     # What a Job of this tool holds on the Site for as long as it runs: one Design Compiler seat.
65:     # The Site declares how many it has under `capacity.licences`, and the count is held across every
66:     # Run of that Site — a licence is the Site's, not a Campaign's. A Site declaring fewer than this
67:     # cannot host the pack, and `/hima pack check` says so before a Campaign exists.
68:     licences:
69:       Design-Compiler: 1
70:     argv:
71:       - make
72:       - -C
73:       - ${WORKSPACE}/flow
74:       - DESIGN=${DESIGN}
75:       - synth
76:       - CLOCK_PERIOD_NS=${PERIOD_NS}
77:       - FORCE_SYNTH=1
78:       - EDA_CONTAINER_NAME=hima-${CAMPAIGN}
79: 
80: # Every rule this pack's judge nodes may apply, by reference. `/hima pack check` resolves each one
81: # against the shipped rules; an unknown id is an error, never a silent pass.
82: rules:
83:   - setup-wns-all-nonnegative
84:   - clock-period-at-most
85: 
86: # What a run of this pack is set to for one generation, and what it may be set to. The strategy is
87: # the pack's, not the harness's: this block is the whole of what a strategy is here, the start form
88: # renders one field per knob, and every value — the form's, `--set`'s, a request body's — is held
89: # against what is declared here before a run starts.
90: #
91: # One knob: the clock period handed to `CLOCK_PERIOD_NS`. Its bounds are wide on purpose — a bound is
92: # what a person could plausibly ask this flow for, not what this design closes at — and they hold
93: # every period this pack has ever been run at, on the stand-in flow and on the reference site.
94: # 0.5 ns is the floor the step-3 acceptance script already refuses below; 10 ns is far above twice
95: # the site's own last result, which is that script's ceiling. A mistyped 0, or a 100, is neither.
96: strategy:
97:   periodNs: { type: number, unit: ns, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2.30 }
98: 
99: # What this pack's numbers are called, for the faces a person reads: one entry per goal parameter the
100: # graph binds and one per knob a run's strategy is made of, each with the label it is read under and
101: # the unit it is measured in — a knob declared as a choice states no unit, because a choice is
102: # measured in nothing. The harness carries the names on the wire whatever is written here — a route
103: # still answers `target_period_ns` and `periodNs` — and the card, the chat's card and `/hima status`
104: # say the words. A goal parameter this block says nothing about is shown under its own name; a knob
105: # it says nothing about is a pack `/hima pack check` refuses.
106: words:
107:   target_period_ns: { label: clock period at most, unit: ns }
108:   periodNs: { label: clock period, unit: ns }

1: # The opene902 timing probe as a HimaFabric graph, and the Loop it explores in: synthesize at the
2: # strategy's clock period, read what it produced, judge it, choose the next strategy — and go round
3: # again with that strategy, generation after generation, until the goal is met, the periods stop
4: # moving, or the campaign's generation limit is spent.
5: #
6: # Four node kinds and no more (CONTEXT.md): act, judge, explore, wait. An act node has one unlabelled
7: # edge out; a judge node's edges carry the outcome they are taken on. A node with no outgoing edge
8: # ends the Run.
9: #
10: # The loop is the last edge below, `next-period` back to `synthesize`, marked `revisit: true` (D43).
11: # Following it is what opens the next generation, with the period the explore node just chose. It is
12: # the only edge in this graph that goes backwards, and the only kind of edge allowed to: a loop a
13: # reader cannot see in this file is a loop the engine would be running behind it.
14: id: opene902-timing-probe
15: version: '2'
16: entry: synthesize
17: 
18: nodes:
19:   # Act: run the pack's tool on the Site, in the Campaign workspace, and wait for it.
20:   - id: synthesize
21:     kind: act
22:     parameters:
23:       tool: synth
24:       # Only the strategy knob is chosen per generation. WORKSPACE, FLOW_ROOT, DESIGN and CAMPAIGN
25:       # are the Run's own workspace and the Site's bindings, which the fabric already holds — and
26:       # which a node may not bind: a pack that named one here would not load.
27:       arguments:
28:         PERIOD_NS: { from: strategy, name: periodNs }
29: 
30:   # Act: read the report that generation produced into HimaLedger, through the contract's own reader.
31:   - id: read-qor
32:     kind: act
33:     parameters:
34:       observes: qorReport
35: 
36:   # Judge: the setup rule first, then the goal rule whose target the Run's goal binds. The outgoing
37:   # edge is chosen by the outcome of the first rule listed.
38:   - id: judge
39:     kind: judge
40:     parameters:
41:       rules:
42:         - setup-wns-all-nonnegative
43:         - clock-period-at-most
44:       bind:
45:         target_period_ns: { from: goal, name: target_period_ns }
46: 
47:   # Method version 2: a met constraint is tested one step tighter; a violation proposes
48:   # period + |slack| - stepNs. This candidate is a hypothesis, not a measured closed period.
49:   # Convergence means the observed periods stopped moving, even if setup still fails.
50:   # Only a generation passing both setup and goal can end goal-met.
51:   # generationLimit is a budget bound, not a claim that the goal is reachable.
52:   - id: next-period
53:     kind: explore
54:     parameters:
55:       chooser: over-constraining-push
56:       bind:
57:         stepNs: 0.05
58:       converge:
59:         read: period
60:         band: 0.05
61:         generations: 1
62:         generationLimit: 6
63: 
64:   # Wait: where a Run stops for a person once its Retry allowance is spent. Nothing draws an edge
65:   # here, and nothing needs to: a Hard blocker is routed to the graph's wait node by the fabric
66:   # itself, exactly as an UNDETERMINED the pack labelled no edge for is. A pack declares where its
67:   # Runs wait; it does not have to draw an edge from every node that might fail.

70:     parameters:

<content>
1: # opene902 timing probe
2: 
3: A HimaPack that answers one question about one design: **which tested clock periods satisfy setup timing, and what should be tried next?** It synthesizes `opene902` at a chosen period in a workspace of its
4: own, reads the qor report the run produced, judges it against the setup constraint and the goal, and
5: chooses the next period to try from what it measured — never from what it hoped. Then it goes round
6: again with that period, and keeps going until the goal is met, the periods stop moving, or the
7: Campaign's generation allowance is spent.
8: 
9: This is the first pack, and it is deliberately the smallest thing that is still a real Campaign: one
10: strategy knob, one tool, one report, two rules, one chooser, one loop. Everything a bigger pack will
11: need — more knobs, more reports, a drill-down loop inside this one — is the same parts with more in
12: each.
13: 
14: Method version **2** changes only the default chooser binding from the legacy `timing-push`
15: guard band to the existing `over-constraining-push` step. Graph and contract both declare version 2.
16: The reference graph topology, tools, reader and Judge rules remain unchanged.
17: 
18: ## What one generation does
19: 
20: 1. **`synthesize`** (act) runs `tools/synth.sh` on the Site: `make … synth` inside the Campaign's own
21:    copy of the flow, at the strategy's clock period, forced so no generation reuses another's
22:    netlist.
23: 2. **`read-qor`** (act) reads `flow/results/<design>/syn/report/qor.rpt` through the
24:    `dc-qor-report@1` reader, which turns it into typed values: setup WNS, setup TNS, the clock
25:    period the run actually used, hold WNS, and cell area.
26: 3. **`judge`** (judge) applies two rules to those values and writes a verdict for each.
27: 4. **`next-period`** (explore) runs the `over-constraining-push` chooser over the verdicts and the values and
28:    records the next strategy with its reasoning.
29: 
30: Then, if the decision was a next period, the Run follows the `revisit` edge from `next-period` back
31: to `synthesize` and does all four again as the next generation, at that period. A `blocked` wait node
32: is declared for the Hard blockers a node's spent Retry allowance produces; nothing draws an edge to
33: it, because the fabric routes a Run there itself.
34: 
35: ## The Campaign: generation after generation
36: 
37: A **generation** is one pass of those four nodes: one synthesis at one period, read, judged, decided.
38: The first is generation one, and every record it leaves — the node transitions, the Job, the
39: observation, the verdicts, the decision — says which generation it belongs to, so the ledger reads as
40: the exploration ran. The Retry allowance is per node *per generation*: a synthesis that failed twice
41: in generation two starts generation three's allowance afresh, because a retry under a new period is
42: not a third go at the old one.
43: 
44: A Campaign of this pack ends in one of four ways, and the run row says which:
45: 
46: - **`ended-goal-met`** — a generation closed its setup timing *and* reached the target period. The
47:   question is answered and no further licence-minute is spent on it.
48: - **`ended-converged`** — the exploration has stopped learning. `next-period` declares what that
49:   means, as data, in the chooser's own vocabulary:
50: 
51:   ```yaml
52:   converge:
53:     read: period        # one of the chooser's own reads
54:     band: 0.05          # ns: how far apart two generations' periods must be to count as movement
55:     generations: 1      # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
56:     generationLimit: 6  # this pack's default allowance, which a person may override
57:   ```
58: 
59:   The 0.05 ns band is the exploration step. This ending states only that consecutive
60:   measured periods moved by less than that band. It does **not** prove the Goal was met,
61:   the last generation met setup, or a global optimum was found. A repeated violation may
62:   converge; use the recorded verdicts to distinguish it from a measured closed result.
63: 
64:   The decision record carries the whole rule — the read, the band, the generations counted, and the
65:   periods compared — so a person can re-derive the ending from one record, and `/hima status` and the
66:   workbench card say it in words.
67: - **`ended-budget-exhausted`** — a meter ran out. `generation-limit` is the Loop's own: the Campaign
68:   reached the generation it was allowed and the revisit that would have opened the next one did not
69:   happen, with the period it would have tried still on record. `time-box` is the other.
70: - **`waiting`** — a node spent its Retry allowance and the Run is at `blocked`, for a person.
71: 
72: The generation limit is a **Budget** meter and not a convergence: convergence is what the exploration
73: learned, the limit is what the Campaign was allowed to spend learning it. `converge.generationLimit`
74: above is this pack's default; `/hima run … --generations <n>` (and the same field on the start route)
75: overrides it, and what the Run is actually held to is on its Budget from the moment it opens.
76: 
77: The local Site generates **stand-in** reports, with `setup_wns = min(0, period − 2.20)` ns.
78: These are controlled test numbers, not measured Design Compiler or silicon improvements.
79: From 2.30 ns, method 2 gives the following bounded examples:
80: 
81: | Goal | Measured periods (ns) | Ending |
82: | --- | --- | --- |
83: | 2.25 ns | 2.30, 2.25 | goal met; the last generation passes both rules |
84: | 2.00 ns | 2.30, 2.25, 2.20, 2.15, 2.15 | converged; the last two generations violate setup and the Goal remains unmet |
85: | 2.00 ns, one generation allowed, starting at 2.00 | 2.00 | generation limit; no measured setup-PASS result exists |
86: 
87: For the converged example, the best **measured setup-PASS** period is 2.20 ns. The 2.15 ns
88: requested period is a violation, and `period + |slack|` is a hypothesis about a possible period,
89: not a new measurement. An unexecuted next Strategy must never be included among measured results.
90: If there is no completed setup-PASS observation, there is no measured closed result to report.
91: The report's generation rows, verdicts, observation IDs and raw qor/logs provide the evidence;
92: this Pack does not add a second best-result computation to the Harness.
93: 
94: ## The goal template
95: 
96: A Campaign binds one number when it starts:
97: 
98: ```
99: target_period_ns = <the clock period this design must close on, in ns>
100: ```
101: 
102: That number is bound into the goal rule `clock-period-at-most@1`, whose predicate is
103: `clock_period ≤ target_period_ns`. The rule file states the comparison; the Campaign states the
104: target. One rule therefore serves every target period, and the run cannot widen its own goal to
105: manufacture a pass — the bound value lands on the verdict, where a person can read what was actually
106: asked for.
107: 
108: `target_period_ns` is the name the harness carries it under; what a person reads is the words this
109: pack declares for it under `words:` in `contract.yml` — **clock period at most**, in **ns**. So a
110: card and `/hima status` say `goal: clock period at most 2.3 ns`, not `goal: target_period_ns=2.3`,
111: while every route still answers under the name. The number keeps whatever precision it was given: a
112: face shows what the ledger holds and rounds nothing. A pack that declares no words for a number shows
113: it under the name; this one declares both of its numbers, this and the strategy knob below.
114: 
115: The setup constraint is the same one step 1 checks, unparameterised:
116: `setup-wns-all-nonnegative@1`, `setup_wns ≥ 0` over all paths. A generation that closes its own
117: setup timing but misses the target is a real result, not a failure: it says the design closes, but
118: not yet where the goal is.
119: 
120: The judge applies the rules in the order `graph.yml` lists them, and the outgoing edge is chosen by
121: the outcome of the **first** — the setup rule. The goal rule decides whether the Campaign is done,
122: not which way the graph goes.
123: 
124: ## The strategy knob
125: 
126: One knob: **`periodNs`**, the clock period handed to `CLOCK_PERIOD_NS` for that generation. It is
127: the only thing that changes between generations of this pack. The flow accepts it as a command-line
128: variable, so nothing in the flow is edited to try a new value.
129: 
130: The knob is this pack's, declared in `contract.yml` under `strategy:` with everything about it in
131: one place — its type, its unit, its bounds and the value a campaign starts at:
132: 
133: ```yaml
134: strategy:
135:   periodNs: { type: number, unit: ns, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2.30 }
136: ```
137: 
138: The bounds are what a person could plausibly ask *this flow* for and not what this design closes at:
139: they hold every period this pack has been run at on the stand-in and on the reference site, and they
140: refuse a mistyped `0` or `100` before a campaign exists, in the same words at the window's start
141: form, at `--set periodNs=<ns>` and in a request body. The default is what the start form fills in
142: and what a run that sets nothing is started at.
143: 
144: Its words, declared beside the goal parameter's under `words:`, are **clock period** in **ns**: a
145: face says `strategy: clock period 2.25 ns`, and the run row and the routes go on carrying
146: `periodNs`.
147: 
148: The period a generation was judged on is read back from the report (`clock_period`), never assumed
149: from the number that was asked for. A tool that silently clamped the period, or a reused netlist from
150: an earlier run, would otherwise be judged as if it had honoured the request.
151: 
152: ## The chooser and its exploration step
153: 
154: `over-constraining-push` uses **stepNs = 0.05 ns**. Given the recorded setup verdict,
155: goal verdict, `clock_period` and `setup_wns`:
156: 
157: - **Both PASS**: end goal-met; do not propose another experiment.
158: - **Setup PASS, Goal not met**: try `clock_period − stepNs`. A met constraint does not
159:   need to expose positive slack for exploration to continue.
160: - **Setup FAIL**: try `clock_period + |setup_wns| − stepNs`. This is a proposed experiment,
161:   not evidence that the design closes at the inferred period.
162: 
163: Goal-met is checked first, then the Pack's convergence rule, then a next Strategy.
164: The chooser remains deterministic YAML in `choosers/over-constraining-push.yml`;
165: no model participates in this sample's strategy selection. The Ledger decision records its
166: inputs, parameters and cited verdicts/observation. Broader AI research belongs to the later Pack.
167: 
168: ### Why the default changed
169: 
170: The historical Step 3 reference-site trace reported zero setup slack at met constraints.
171: The old `timing-push` PASS clause therefore increased the requested period by 0.05 ns every
172: generation. On the calibrated stand-in, starting at 2.30 ns produces 2.30, 2.35, 2.40,
173: 2.45, 2.50, 2.55 and stops at the generation limit. That failure remains an explicitly
174: named `legacy-timing-push-probe` test variant; the old chooser file is retained unchanged.
175: 
176: Version 2 avoids relying on positive margin in that case. The local examples prove the
177: mechanism under their stated arithmetic, not a universal property of Design Compiler, all
178: designs or synthesis settings. Real Site efficacy requires a separate measured validation.
179: Historical records belong to their original method version and must not be relabeled as v2.
180: 
181: ## What a Site must bind
182: 
183: `contract.yml` names three inputs; a Site binds them in its own file under `bindings:`.
184: 
185: | Input | On `linglong` | On the local site |
186: | --- | --- | --- |
187: | `flowRoot` | `/data/eda/project/design_zoo` — the Site's Design Zoo | the generated stand-in flow |
188: | `design` | `opene902` | `opene902` |
189: | `workspaceRoot` | `/data/eda/project/hima_harness` | the isolated home's workspace |
190: 
191: Nothing else about the pack changes between the two. That is what the run contract is for:
192: `/hima pack check opene902-timing-probe --site <site>` says, before anything runs, whether a Site can
193: host this pack — every input bound, every tool's first word a wrapper the Permit allows, every rule
194: and reader resolvable, and every licence a tool holds declared by the Site in at least that number.
195: 
196: ## What a generation holds
197: 
198: `synth` holds **one `Design-Compiler` seat** for as long as its Job runs, declared on the tool in
199: `contract.yml`. A Site says how many seats it has under `capacity.licences` — `linglong` declares 99
200: — and the count is held across every Run of that Site, exactly as the parallel job cap is, because a
201: licence belongs to the Site and not to a Campaign. A launch that would take one seat too many waits
202: for one to come free, and says so on the node; a Site that declares fewer seats than this tool holds
203: (or none, which is what a node-locked tool's `0` means) cannot host the pack at all, and the check
204: says so rather than letting a Run wait for a seat that will never come free.
205: 
206: The other tool a person might expect here — Innovus — is not in this pack, which is why nothing
207: declares the reference site's `Innovus_Impl_System: 0`.
208: 
209: ## Where a generation runs
210: 
211: Never in `flowRoot`. `/hima pack prepare` copies the flow's makefile, its `flows/` and `manifests/`
212: directories, and the design's `build/` and `sources/` trees (about 56 MB for `opene902`) into
213: `<workspaceRoot>/<campaign>/flow/`, and every generation of that Campaign runs there. The flow
214: derives its project root from its own location, so the copy builds into the copy.
215: 
216: The one thing that does *not* follow from the copy's location is the container the flow's wrapper
217: runs in: it creates a container by name and binds the project root into it, so a copy run under the
218: Site's own container name would write the Site's own results after all. Hence
219: `EDA_CONTAINER_NAME=hima-<campaign>` on every tool line, and the container's name recorded in the
220: workspace's `workspace.json` so a later cleanup knows what to remove.
221: 
222: ## What the Campaign leaves for the next one
223: 
224: Every ended Run of this pack writes its own technical report into the Campaign workspace, beside the
225: results: `<workspaceRoot>/<campaign>/hima-experience/<runId>.md` for the people who read it and
226: `<runId>.json` for the programs that do. Nothing in this pack's three files asks for it — the harness
227: writes it for every pack, whatever ending the Run reached, a cancel and a spent time box included —
228: and it is written where the results are and left there, because the evidence of a Campaign belongs to
229: the Site owner and outlives the session that produced it. HimaLedger keeps only each file's path,
230: size and SHA-256, so a person who fetches one months later can hold it against what the Campaign
231: actually wrote.
232: 
233: What the Markdown holds is this pack's own story: the ending and why, the goal that was bound and
234: the Site it ran on, every Budget meter against its bound, one row per generation with the period it
235: asked for, the period and slack it measured, its verdicts and its decision, then a paragraph per
236: generation saying the same in sentences — *It asked the flow for 2.25 ns and measured 2.25 ns, with
237: 0.00 ns of setup slack. HimaJudge found PASS on setup-wns-all-nonnegative, FAIL on
238: clock-period-at-most. The decision was …* — and finally the path the Run took, any Hard blockers,
239: and any cancel. So the file answers, without the ledger, the two questions a pack author is asked
240: about a Campaign that has finished: what did it learn, and why did it stop.
241: 
242: A person reads it in three places without going to the Site: the card's evidence drawer on an ended
243: Run, the `.md` route the drawer links to, and `/hima status <run>`, which names both paths.

(End of file - total 243 lines)
</content>

<content>
1: # The chooser of a timing push that knows its business: it over-constrains on purpose and reads the
2: # violation the tool answers with. Data, never code (D38), beside `timing-push.yml`, for a pack whose
3: # knob is a clock period judged against a setup constraint.
4: #
5: # Why a second push rule exists at all (D45). `timing-push` asks a met period how much margin it had
6: # and pushes by the answer. A tool that reports no margin for a met period does not answer that
7: # question: it states a setup slack of exactly 0.00 whenever the period it was given is met, because
8: # it stops optimizing the moment the constraint is satisfied. So on such a tool that clause reads
9: # `period − 0 + guardBand` and loosens the period by the guard band every generation, which is the
10: # trace the step-3 acceptance on the reference site recorded (D45) — six generations walking from
11: # 2.28 ns out to 2.53 ns, converging on nothing.
12: #
13: # The method here never asks a met period what it had to spare. It asks for less than it believes is
14: # possible and lets the tool say by how much it was wrong:
15: #
16: # - The constraint PASSED — the tool said nothing about the margin, because a met period is all it
17: #   says. Take one step tighter and ask again; that is the over-constraining, and `stepNs` is how
18: #   coarse the walk in is.
19: # - The constraint FAILED — now the tool has stated something: the design missed by `|slack|`, so
20: #   `period + |slack|` is the period it can actually close at. Ask for one step less than that. The
21: #   next generation misses by that same step, states the same achievable period, and asks for the
22: #   same number again — two successive generations asking and measuring the same period, which is
23: #   what a pack's `converge:` calls having stopped learning. The violation is on record, which is
24: #   the fact the Campaign was run to find.
25: # - Both the constraint and the goal PASSED — the design closed and reached what the Run was for.
26: #   There is no next strategy; the decision is that the Goal is met.
27: #
28: # So a Campaign on this chooser ends `ended-goal-met` when the goal is reachable and
29: # `ended-converged` one step below the achievable period when it is not, on a tool that reports zero
30: # slack for a met period and on one that reports a real margin alike: the PASS clause never reads the
31: # margin, so it cannot be misled by a tool that has none to give.
32: id: over-constraining-push
33: version: '1'
34: title: Over-constrain the clock period by one step and read the violation
35: 
36: # The one number a pack binds, in its explore node's `bind:`: how far the walk in moves each
37: # generation while nothing is violated, and how far above the violated period the exploration settles.
38: parameter:
39:   name: stepNs
40:   unit: ns
41: 
42: # What is read out of the Run's latest observation, exactly as `timing-push` reads it: the period is
43: # the one the report stated and never the one the Run asked for, so a tool that clamped the period is
44: # not pushed against as if it had honoured the request.
45: reads:
46:   period: { type: clock_period, unit: ns }
47:   slack: { type: setup_wns, unit: ns }
48: 
49: # First matching `when` wins. `constraint` is the verdict of the judge node's first rule — the one
50: # the outgoing edge was chosen by — and `goal` the verdict of its goal rule.
51: # `next` sets the pack's own strategy knobs by name, and a knob it does not name carries over. This
52: # chooser is for a pack whose knob is a clock period; the name below is the one such a contract
53: # declares it under, and `/hima pack check` holds the two against each other before a campaign runs.
54: decide:
55:   - when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
56:     goalMet: true
57:   - when: { constraint: PASS }
58:     next:
59:       periodNs: { sum: [period, { neg: stepNs }] }
60:   - when: { constraint: FAIL }
61:     next:
62:       periodNs: { sum: [period, { abs: slack }, { neg: stepNs }] }

(End of file - total 62 lines)
</content>

1: #!/bin/sh
2: # The `synth` tool of the opene902 timing probe: one synthesis generation at a chosen clock period.
3: #
4: # The command line below is the one `contract.yml` declares for this tool, so a person can reproduce
5: # a generation by hand exactly as HimaFabric runs it:
6: #
7: #   WORKSPACE=/data/eda/project/hima_harness/<campaign> \
8: #   FLOW_ROOT=/data/eda/project/design_zoo \
9: #   DESIGN=opene902 PERIOD_NS=2.20 CAMPAIGN=<campaign> \
10: #   sh packs/opene902-timing-probe/tools/synth.sh
11: #
12: # Three things about that line are the whole point of it:
13: #   - `-C "$WORKSPACE/flow"` runs the Campaign's own copy of the flow. The flow derives its project
14: #     root from its own location, so the copy builds into the copy and the Site's own results under
15: #     $FLOW_ROOT are never written.
16: #   - `FORCE_SYNTH=1` because the flow reuses an existing netlist otherwise, and a generation that
17: #     reused the previous one's netlist would be judged on a period it never ran at.
18: #   - `EDA_CONTAINER_NAME=hima-$CAMPAIGN` because the flow's wrapper CREATES a container of that name
19: #     on first use and binds $PROJECT_ROOT into it. Running the copy under the Site's own container
20: #     name would bind the Site's flow instead and write the Site's results (D19).
21: set -eu
22: 
23: : "${WORKSPACE:?the Campaign workspace on the Site}"
24: : "${FLOW_ROOT:?the Site's flow root, for the record: the generation runs in the workspace copy}"
25: : "${DESIGN:?the design to synthesize}"
26: : "${PERIOD_NS:?the clock period this generation is the strategy for}"
27: : "${CAMPAIGN:?the Campaign this generation belongs to, which names its container}"
28: 
29: exec make -C "$WORKSPACE/flow" DESIGN="$DESIGN" synth CLOCK_PERIOD_NS="$PERIOD_NS" FORCE_SYNTH=1 EDA_CONTAINER_NAME="hima-$CAMPAIGN"

1: # The value types the readers this bundle ships emit, and what each one is measured in (#61).
2: #
3: # This is the *default* vocabulary and not the vocabulary: a HimaPack carries a `semantics.yml` of
4: # its own beside its `contract.yml`, resolved ahead of this file, so a pack whose method yields a
5: # candidate count or an adoption ratio declares it where the method lives (D46). What is here is what
6: # every pack of this kind would otherwise write out again — the base timing quantities the bundled
7: # readers read out of a synthesis or a post-route report — and nothing else.
8: #
9: # Every reader's output is held against the resolved list before it reaches HimaLedger: the type
10: # declared, the unit the declared one, `mode` and `scope` carried exactly where they are declared.
11: # The four slack types are the ones that carry both, because a slack is a statement about one

1: # The chooser of the opene902 timing probe, and of any pack whose knob is a clock period judged
2: # against a setup constraint. Data, never code (D38): a person adjusts the push rule here, beside
3: # the judge rules, without reading TypeScript.
4: #
5: # - The constraint PASSED — the design closed with slack to spare. Push: the next period is the
6: #   period the report stated, minus that slack, plus the guard band. Taking the whole slack back
7: #   would land exactly on the edge the tool just reported, which is where estimation error lives.
8: # - The constraint FAILED — the design missed by the slack it reported. Back off by exactly that
9: #   much, plus the guard band.
10: # - Both the constraint and the goal PASSED — the design closed and reached what the Run was for.
11: #   There is no next strategy; the decision is that the Goal is met.
12: id: timing-push
13: version: '1'
14: title: Push the clock period against the measured setup margin
15: 
16: # The one number a pack binds, in its explore node's `bind:`. What the chooser leaves on the table on
17: # purpose is the pack author's judgement, not this file's.
18: parameter:
19:   name: guardBandNs
20:   unit: ns
21: 
22: # What is read out of the Run's latest observation. The period is read from the report, never from
23: # the number the Run asked for: a tool that clamped the period, or a netlist reused from an earlier
24: # generation, would otherwise be pushed against as if it had honoured the request.
25: reads:
26:   period: { type: clock_period, unit: ns }
27:   slack: { type: setup_wns, unit: ns }
28: 
29: # First matching `when` wins. `constraint` is the verdict of the judge node's first rule — the one
30: # the outgoing edge was chosen by — and `goal` the verdict of its goal rule. A generation no clause
31: # matches is answered with a reason, never with a period computed from a substituted zero.
32: # `next` sets the pack's own strategy knobs by name, and a knob it does not name carries over. This
33: # chooser is for a pack whose knob is a clock period; the name below is the one such a contract
34: # declares it under, and `/hima pack check` holds the two against each other before a campaign runs.
35: decide:
36:   - when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
37:     goalMet: true
38:   - when: { constraint: PASS }
39:     next:
40:       periodNs: { sum: [period, { neg: slack }, guardBandNs] }
41:   - when: { constraint: FAIL }
42:     next:
43:       periodNs: { sum: [period, { abs: slack }, guardBandNs] }
